Subject: Re: Fwd: Model cutover today - sudden P95/P99 spike

Initial triage: we pulled canary traces and short-lived tail logs. Observations:
- KV cache miss rate jumped ~12x starting at 07:46 PT when canary traffic ramped. Prefix cache warmup didn't happen as expected.
- Average batching window increased: median batch size rose from 6->14 concurrent requests causing queueing on the runtime worker.
- Model variant redwood-v8-quant appears to have ~30% longer token decode latency on cold KV misses vs v7.
- No obvious infra node OOMs; GPU utilization is nominal but the async queue length is high.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Traffic shift: move the account back to v7 baseline (rollback canary) — lowest blast radius.
2) Reduce canary concurrency cap and limit live batching for this tenant (short-term throttle).
3) Enable aggressive prefix cache seeding for Stormfront session prefixes (requires a warmup job).

I recommend option 1 now. I'll prepare the rollback steps — need Platform Ops approval. Attaching canary_trace_logs_20280903.tar.gz with samples.

—Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Michael / Claire — rollback to redwood-v7 completed at 10:02 PT. Post-shift summary:
- P95 returned to baseline (~210–240ms) within ~6 minutes of rollback.
- P99 reduced to near-normal levels (~420–600ms).
- Error rate dropped back to baseline. Throughput recovered.

We’ve started a mitigation playbook: hold rollouts for Stormfront, run focused warmup for KV prefixes, and run an internal perf comparison between v7 and v8-quant on cold-paths. Customer success will follow-up on credits and a 48-hour technical deep dive meeting.

Links: post-rollback metrics: https://redwood.app/dashboards/stormfront-case-2893
